title: Leorio vs Kurapika: The Fight That Almost Sank Them Before The Hunter Exam

cuts.raw_narration: Inside the ship's cabin, the bearded captain has pulled Gon aside to demand why he wants to be a hunter. Gon, the spiky-haired boy in green, looks up at the older man and answers cheerfully and without hesitation: his dad is a hunter, and being a hunter was the most important thing in the world to his father, so he wants to find out why. The camera holds on Gon's bright, open face and then cuts to the captain listening in silhouette, his expression softening as he realizes who this boy is.

Later, the captain turns the same question on the blond boy in the blue tabard, Kurapika. Standing beside a rain-streaked window with Leorio and Gon watching in the background, Kurapika answers flatly that he is the sole survivor of the Kurta clan — four years ago his entire clan was annihilated by a band of criminals — and that is why he wants to become a hunter: to capture the Phantom Troupe. Leorio, the older teen in the blue suit, and Gon both turn to stare at him in shock.

The captain then asks Leorio why HE wants to be a hunter. Leorio, grinning smugly, spreads his hands and says it's simple — for the money, a big mansion, a cool car. Kurapika, eyes closed, cuts in with a dry insult: if only money could buy class. Leorio snaps. He whips around, jabs a finger at Kurapika and snarls at him to step outside — time to finish off the filthy Kurta bloodline once and for all. He storms out of the cabin. Kurapika's eyes fly open and flash a burning scarlet as he calls after him: 'Take that back, Leorio!'

As Leorio and Kurapika square off outside, Gon stays behind, calm. In a warm-lit flashback he remembers Aunt Mito at their kitchen table on Whale Island, telling him you can never understand a person unless you understand what makes them angry — that is how you get to know someone. Cut back to the ship, Gon quietly decides that whatever the two of them are so upset about must be really important to them, and there is nothing to do now but stay out of the way.

But the fight never happens. A massive waterspout has closed on the ship. The captain shouts orders, sailors scramble in the pouring rain, and out on the rolling deck a crewman loses his footing on the wet planks and is swept toward the railing, about to be flung overboard.

The storm has passed. On the drenched deck, the rescued sailor in the orange shirt and blue bandana stands facing Leorio, Kurapika and Gon, grinning with relief. He tells them they caught him together — they saved his life. Gon beams up at him. The sailor then bows deeply to Kurapika and Leorio in thanks. Kurapika closes his eyes and politely tells him no thanks are necessary, and Leorio, thrown by the gratitude, scratches the back of his head with a wide, sheepish grin.

The sailor heads back to his post. Alone with Leorio, Kurapika suddenly laughs at himself — he's embarrassed at his own rudeness earlier — and gives a small, sincere bow: 'Pardon my rudeness, Mr. Leorio.' Leorio, caught off guard, looks down and mutters that he wasn't expecting that; she can drop the 'Mr.' — Leorio is fine. Then, quieter, he offers his own apology: 'I'm sorry too. I take back everything I said to you before. That was wrong of me.' Kurapika, standing beside him on the sunlit deck, gives him a warm, closed-eyed smile.

The captain has been watching from the cabin doorway with a bottle in his hand. He steps out and tells the three of them, with a gap-toothed grin, that they're growing on him — so he'll make sure all three of them get safely dropped off at the port closest to the exam site. Leorio blinks and asks about the test. The captain laughs: it's like he said, HE decides who goes on to take the exam. Congratulations — all three of them are moving on. Gon punches the air with both fists and jumps for joy on the deck as Kurapika and Leorio stand beside him under a clear blue sky.
